I need to identify likely markers that define boundaries. It seems 3 is used to color areas enclosed by 9s. I’ll mark the changes in the grid, noting where 3s appear in relation to the 9s, which act as boundaries. I’ll need to request a more detailed demonstration.

grid=[[8]*8 for _ in range(30)]
pts=[(1,6),(3,7),(5,0),(5,7),(9,2),(12,2),(12,4),(17,6),(20,7),(21,5)]
for r,c in pts:grid[r][c]=7
out=[row[:] for row in grid]
for r in range(len(grid)):
 cs=[c for rr,c in pts if rr==r]
 for a,b in zip(cs,cs[1:]):
  for c in range(a+1,b):out[r][c]=3
for c in range(len(grid[0])):
 rs=[r for r,cc in pts if cc==c]
 for a,b in zip(rs,rs[1:]):
  for r in range(a+1,b):out[r][c]=3
print('\n'.join(' '.join(map(str,row)) for row in out))
# save required transform
from pathlib import Path
p=Path('/home/USER/continual-arc-baselines/.workbench/stage1/HPL0-prime-agent-luna6-low-fresh0/frozen/seen-reference-3/play/users/u053/system/state/workspace/programs/task-9f855a99.py')
p.parent.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
p.write_text('''def transform(grid):\n    out = [row[:] for row in grid]\n    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])\n    for r in range(h):\n        cols = [c for c, v in enumerate(grid[r]) if v != grid[0][0]]\n        for a, b in zip(cols, cols[1:]):\n            for c in range(a + 1, b): out[r][c] = 3\n    for c in range(w):\n        rows = [r for r in range(h) if grid[r][c] != grid[0][0]]\n        for a, b in zip(rows, rows[1:]):\n            for r in range(a + 1, b): out[r][c] = 3\n    return out\n''')
